Parcelbird
Board (two founders, two investors)

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Do not launch Parcelbird Now in 2027; scale the software for grocers instead
Quick commerce is growing fast, but no operator has yet made it pay
–	US quick-commerce sales grew 2.8 times from 2022 to 2025
–	Both incumbents lose money on every order; QuickBasket closed 4 of 11 cities
Every order loses money at benchmark economics; the plan needs inputs no site has reached
–	At the benchmark median, each order loses $6.17 after store costs
–	The plan beats the best site on all four inputs; break-even needs a $47 order
The Columbus pop-up fell short of the benchmark, and lasting customers are costly to win
–	Promotions explain almost half of the pop-up's extra loss per order
–	Only 22% of customers stayed to month three, and each cost $173 to win
Even if it goes to plan, the launch breaks the 12-month runway floor
–	The plan leaves about 6 months of runway at month 18; at median economics nine stores lose $18M a year
Scaling the software is the better use of cash; revisit operating once three conditions hold
–	About 10 new contracts pay for the $0.8M a year of hires the software needs
–	Revisit when a network site makes money after store costs
